mainTopic: Using impure תרומה safely, the replanted saplings משנה, and whether היסח הדעת is פסול טומאה or פסול הגוף
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier answer. Impure תרומה may be burned as fuel only when it is בשליקתא ומאיסתא (boiled and made repulsive), so no one will come to eat it. The גמרא shows that רב אשי first said this about אבא שאול, the dough-kneader in רבי's house. Next, רבא בר מתנה asks about a משנה in תרומות. Impure תרומה saplings that were replanted no longer pass on טומאה, yet they are still forbidden to eat. Why? The students first answer in רבה's name that they are forbidden only to זרים. רבא בר מתנה shows that this reading would make the משנה repeat rules already taught, and the students fall silent. He then quotes רב ששת: the saplings are forbidden even to כהנים because of היסח הדעת. That answer leads to the dispute between רבי יוחנן (היסח הדעת is פסול טומאה) and ריש לקיש (it is פסול הגוף), tested by whether we would listen to אליהו. רבי יוחנן then challenges ריש לקיש from a ברייתא about disqualified bird חטאות that were left until their form decayed, and he begins quoting a משנה whose rule appears on the next amud.

steps.title: Only boiled and repulsive wheat may be used
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer. The impure תרומה being used here is boiled and repulsive, just like in the case where רב אשי gave this answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Just as there, it means wheat that was] boiled and repulsive, so too here, it means boiled and repulsive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is completing an answer that began on the previous page. It applies רב אשי's explanation to the current case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that someone using impure תרומה might come to eat it by mistake (a תקלה). The answer is that the wheat was first boiled and made disgusting, so no one would ever eat it. The same solution that worked in another case is applied here.

keyTerms.meaning: boiled (wheat that was cooked until it is useless for eating)

phrases.english: [there it refers to wheat that is] boiled and repulsive,
phrases.notes: Continues a sentence from the previous daf.

phrases.english: so too here, it is boiled and repulsive.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an answer begun on the previous daf.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) to wheat that cannot be eaten.
steps.terutzMaskana: Impure תרומה may be used only in a form that cannot lead to eating it.

steps.title: Where was רב אשי's statement originally said?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the original setting of רב אשי's explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where was רב אשי's statement said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא just quoted רב אשי. Now it asks where he originally said this. This sets up the next step, which brings the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new about the law is being challenged here. The גמרא only wants to identify the original context of the quote it just used.

phrases.english: And where was [the statement] of Rav Ashi said?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the explanation used in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The original context of רב אשי's statement.

steps.title: The story of אבא שאול the kneader
steps.stepSummary: The source is a report from רבי יצחק: in רבי's house, water for kneading pure dough was heated using impure תרומה wheat as fuel.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said about this: רבי אבין בר רב אחא said in the name of רבי יצחק: אבא שאול was the dough-kneader of רבי's house. They would heat water for him using impure תרומה wheat, so that he could knead dough in purity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by telling the story where רב אשי's explanation first came up. In this story, impure תרומה wheat was burned as fuel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Impure תרומה cannot be eaten, but it may be burned as fuel. רש"י explains that רבי's household bought this wheat cheaply from כהנים. Here it was used as fuel to heat water for pure dough. This case will raise the worry addressed in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: impure תרומה, which may not be eaten but may be burned

phrases.aramaic: אַהָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין בַּר רַב אַחָא
phrases.english: On this, which Rabbi Avin bar Rav Acha said
that Rabbi Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּא שָׁאוּל גַּבָּל שֶׁל בֵּית רַבִּי הָיָה,
phrases.english: Abba Shaul was the dough-kneader of Rabbi's household,
and they would heat hot water for him
with wheat of impure teruma
phrases.notes: The wheat was used as fuel.

phrases.english: to knead dough with it in purity.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַהָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין בַּר רַב אַחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The statement was said about the case of אבא שאול in רבי's house.

steps.title: Isn't there a risk someone will eat the wheat?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the practice: keeping impure תרומה wheat around could lead someone to eat it by mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why [was this allowed]? We should worry that it might lead to a stumbling block!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the practice in רבי's house. It worries that someone might accidentally eat the impure wheat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating impure תרומה is forbidden. If the wheat is lying around looking like normal wheat, someone could take it and eat it. That accident is called a תקלה.

keyTerms.meaning: a stumbling block, an accidental sin

phrases.english: Why?

phrases.aramaic: נֵיחוּשׁ דִּילְמָא אָתֵי בְּהוּ לִידֵי תַקָּלָה!
phrases.english: Let us worry lest they come through it to a stumbling block!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי? נֵיחוּשׁ דִּילְמָא אָתֵי בְּהוּ לִידֵי תַקָּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the practice described in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The practice of using impure תרומה wheat as fuel.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Edible-looking impure תרומה could be eaten by mistake.

steps.title: רב אשי: the wheat was boiled and repulsive
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the wheat was boiled and made disgusting, so no one would eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: [It was wheat that was] boiled and repulsive.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the challenge. This is the original place of the line quoted in step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wheat that is boiled and repulsive is no longer food in anyone's eyes, so there is no risk of a תקלה. The use is still allowed, but only in this form.
steps.whatToRemember: Impure תרומה may be used for fuel, but only once it is in a form no one would eat (בשליקתא ומאיסתא).

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
[It was] boiled and repulsive.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wheat was inedible, so there was no risk of a תקלה.

steps.title: רבא בר מתנה asks what רבה taught about תרומות
steps.stepSummary: Two students who learned מסכת תרומות in רבה's school meet רבא בר מתנה. He asks them what they learned there.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי בר אבין and רב חנניא בר אבין learned [מסכת] תרומות in רבה's house. רבא בר מתנה met them and said to them: What do you say about תרומות in the Master's house?
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins about another law of impure תרומה. רבא בר מתנה opens a conversation, which sets up his question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He is not yet asking anything specific. He wants to hear how רבה explained the מסכת, as a lead-in to the difficulty he has in mind.

keyTerms.meaning: the house (study hall) of the Master

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּיֵי בַּר אָבִין וְרַב חֲנַנְיָא בַּר אָבִין
phrases.english: Abaye bar Avin and Rav Chananya bar Avin
learned Terumot in Rabba's house.
Rava bar Matna met them,
he said to them:
What do you say about Terumot of the Master's house?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic that is linked by the theme of impure תרומה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What explanations רבה taught in מסכת תרומות.

steps.title: The students ask what is bothering him
steps.stepSummary: The students ask him to state his specific difficulty.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: And what is difficult for you?
steps.whatsHappening: The students ask רבא בר מתנה what problem he has in mind. This sets up his challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They understand that his general question hides a specific difficulty. They ask him to say it outright.

phrases.english: They said to him:
And what is difficult for you?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to step 6 by asking for the specific difficulty.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly is troubling רבא בר מתנה.

steps.title: If the replanted saplings are pure, why can't they be eaten?
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר מתנה quotes a משנה: impure תרומה saplings that were replanted no longer pass on טומאה, yet they are forbidden to eat. He asks why.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: We learned [in a משנה]: Saplings of תרומה that became impure and were planted are pure in that they do not make things impure, but they are forbidden to eat (as תרומה). Since they are pure and do not make things impure, why are they forbidden to eat?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר מתנה states his difficulty. The משנה seems to contradict itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Planting the saplings in the ground removes their טומאה. If they are now pure, the only reason to forbid impure תרומה is gone. So why does the משנה still forbid eating them?

keyTerms.meaning: pure in that they do not pass on impurity

phrases.english: He said to them, we learned:
Saplings of teruma that became impure and he planted them —
are pure, not imparting impurity,
and are forbidden to be eaten (as teruma).
But since they are pure, not imparting impurity,
why are they forbidden to be eaten?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מֵאַחַר דִּטְהוֹרִין מִלְּטַמֵּא, אַמַּאי אֲסוּרִין מִלֶּאֱכוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the difficulty that step 7 asked for.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה in תרומות about replanted impure saplings.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Once their טומאה is gone, there is no reason left to forbid eating them.

steps.title: רבה: forbidden only to non-כהנים
steps.stepSummary: The students answer in רבה's name. 'Forbidden' means forbidden to זרים, because the saplings are still תרומה. A כהן may eat them.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: This is what רבה said: What does 'forbidden' mean? Forbidden to non-כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The students give רבה's answer. The ban in the משנה is not because of טומאה. It is because the saplings are still תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Planting removed the טומאה, but it did not remove the status of תרומה. That is why a זר still may not eat them, while a כהן may.

keyTerms.meaning: non-כהנים, who may not eat תרומה

steps.confusionAlert: 'Forbidden to eat' here does not mean forbidden to everyone. It means forbidden to non-כהנים, because the produce is still תרומה.

phrases.english: They said to him, this is what Rabba said:
What does 'forbidden' mean —
forbidden to non-priests.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a word in the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Forbidden' seemed to mean forbidden to everyone because of טומאה.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means forbidden only to זרים, because the saplings are still תרומה.

steps.title: The rule 'growths of תרומה are תרומה' is already taught
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר מתנה objects: if that is the point, the משנה teaches nothing new. We already learned that what grows from תרומה is תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is it teaching us? That the growths of תרומה are תרומה? We already learned: the growths of תרומה are תרומה!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר מתנה attacks רבה's answer. With that reading, the משנה would just be repeating a rule taught elsewhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה is not supposed to repeat itself for no reason. If the only point is that the new growth keeps its תרומה status, that is already stated in another משנה, so the reading seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: what is it teaching us (what is new)?

phrases.english: And what does it teach us:
that the growths of teruma are teruma?
We already learned: growths of teruma are teruma!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's answer from step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's reading that 'forbidden' means forbidden to זרים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה would be repeating a rule that is already taught elsewhere.

steps.title: Maybe it means growths of growths, from a seed that stays whole
steps.stepSummary: A possible defense is raised: perhaps the משנה means second-generation growths, from a plant whose seed does not break down in the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say it means growths of growths, and what does it teach us? [That the rule applies] to something whose seed does not disintegrate.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר מתנה himself suggests a defense ('and if you say'), in order to knock it down in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some plants, like onions, do not lose their original seed when planted. The new idea would be that even the growths of growths of such a plant stay תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: a plant whose seed does not disintegrate

phrases.english: And if you say [it means] growths of growths,
and what does it teach us —
[the case of] an item whose seed does not disintegrate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a possible defense against step 10's objection.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Hypothetical אוקימתא, raised in order to reject it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה would be teaching about growths of growths of a plant whose seed stays whole.

steps.title: The growths-of-growths rule is also already taught
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר מתנה rejects that defense: a משנה about טבל already teaches that when the seed does not disintegrate, even growths of growths keep the original status.
steps.simpleTranslation: We also learned this: טבל — its growths are permitted when it is a plant whose seed disintegrates. But a plant whose seed does not disintegrate — even its growths of growths are forbidden to eat.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר מתנה rejects the defense he just raised. That rule is also already known from another משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה about טבל already teaches the principle that a lasting seed passes on its status even to growths of growths. So this second reading also leaves our משנה with nothing new to teach.

phrases.english: This too we already learned:
Untithed produce — its growths are permitted,
in an item whose seed disintegrates.
But in an item whose seed does not disintegrate —
even growths of growths are forbidden to eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the defense offered in step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The growths-of-growths reading of the משנה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That rule is already taught in the משנה about טבל, so it would be a repetition.

steps.title: The students fall silent
steps.stepSummary: The students have no answer, so their reading of the משנה falls. Steps 14-15 bring a different explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: They were silent.
steps.whatsHappening: The students cannot answer רבא בר מתנה's challenge, so their reading of the משנה falls. The conversation goes on, and the next step asks רבא בר מתנה for his own explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Silence means רבה's answer, as the students reported it, could not be defended against the charge that it makes the משנה repetitive. The גמרא never rescues this reading. Instead, the next steps bring a different explanation from רב ששת.
steps.whatToRemember: רבה read 'forbidden' as 'forbidden to זרים'. רבא בר מתנה showed that this reading makes the משנה repeat known rules: גידולי תרומה תרומה, and the rule from טבל about a seed that does not disintegrate. The students had no reply.

phrases.english: They were silent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The students cannot answer the rejection in step 12.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבה's reading ('forbidden to זרים') cannot be defended. It is set aside in favor of רב ששת's explanation in step 15.

steps.title: The students ask רבא בר מתנה what he has heard
steps.stepSummary: The students could not answer רבא בר מתנה's objection, so they ask him whether he has a tradition about what 'forbidden' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Have you heard anything about this?
steps.whatsHappening: The students cannot defend their answer, so they turn to רבא בר מתנה and ask whether he knows a better explanation. This line sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their reading ('forbidden to זרים') was shown to teach nothing new. Instead of trying again on their own, they ask for a received teaching. This moves the סוגיא from attack to a new explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Have you heard? Asks whether someone has a received tradition

phrases.english: They said to him:
phrases.notes: The students speak to רבא בר מתנה.

phrases.english: Have you heard anything about this?
phrases.notes: A request for a tradition, not an attack.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the unanswered question in step 13 by asking the questioner himself for an answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבא בר מתנה has a tradition explaining 'forbidden' (אסורין) in the משנה.

steps.title: רב ששת: the saplings are forbidden even to כהנים because of היסח הדעת
steps.stepSummary: Quoting רב ששת, רבא בר מתנה explains that 'forbidden' means forbidden to כהנים, because the saplings became disqualified when the כהן stopped watching them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: This is what רב ששת said: What does 'forbidden' mean? Forbidden to כהנים, since they became disqualified for them through היסח הדעת (the owner no longer paying attention to them).
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר מתנה gives a new explanation from רב ששת. The saplings are forbidden even to כהנים, because once they became טמא the כהן stopped guarding them (היסח הדעת).
steps.deeperAnalysis: תרומה must be watched. If the owner stops paying attention to it (היסח הדעת), it becomes disqualified. Once these saplings became טמא, the כהן stopped guarding them. So even after planting cleans them of their actual טומאה, the disqualification of היסח הדעת remains, and a כהן still may not eat them. This answers the 'nothing new' objection, because now the משנה teaches something we did not know before.

keyTerms.meaning: Removing one's attention: no longer watching or guarding the תרומה
Priests, who may normally eat תרומה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two problems. Planting does clean the saplings of their actual טומאה. The new problem is different: they were left unwatched.
steps.whyThisMatters: It makes היסח הדעת the key idea of the rest of the סוגיא. Everything that follows asks what kind of disqualification היסח הדעת really is.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת:
phrases.english: He said to them: This is what Rav Sheshet said:
What does 'forbidden' mean?
phrases.notes: Points back to the word in the משנה.

phrases.english: Forbidden to priests,
phrases.notes: Not only to non-priests (זרים), but even to כהנים.

phrases.english: since they became disqualified for them through diversion of attention.
phrases.notes: Gives the reason: they were left unguarded.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the students' question in step 14. It also fixes the problem from step 10, where the משנה seemed to teach nothing new.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reading of a word: 'forbidden' is applied to כהנים, not just to זרים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Forbidden' meant forbidden to זרים, which would teach nothing new.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Forbidden' means forbidden even to כהנים, because of היסח הדעת.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב ששת's tradition: the saplings are forbidden to כהנים because of היסח הדעת.

steps.title: This only works if היסח הדעת is a disqualification of its own
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: רב ששת's answer works if היסח הדעת is פסול הגוף. But if it is only a worry about טומאה, planting should remove that worry too.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is fine according to the one who says היסח הדעת is פסול הגוף (a disqualification of its own). But according to the one who says היסח הדעת is פסול טומאה (a worry that it became טמא), what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב ששת's answer. It says the answer only works according to one view of what היסח הדעת is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If היסח הדעת is a separate rabbinic rule (פסול הגוף), planting does not fix it, so the saplings stay forbidden to כהנים. But if היסח הדעת is only a worry that the תרומה became טמא, there is a problem. The משנה says planting purifies saplings that were certainly טמא, so it should surely also remove a mere doubt of טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well for the one who says…; opens a 'fine for one view, but not the other' challenge
A disqualification of its own, not based on any worry about טומאה
A disqualification based on the worry that the item became טמא
What is there to say? Means the view has no answer

steps.confusionAlert: Both views agree that היסח הדעת disqualifies תרומה. They disagree only about why. That reason decides whether planting can fix the problem.

phrases.english: It works well for the one who says
phrases.notes: This starts a familiar pattern: it's fine for one opinion, but what about the other?

phrases.aramaic: הֶיסַּח הַדַּעַת פְּסוּל הַגּוּף הָוֵי — שַׁפִּיר,
phrases.english: diversion of attention is an inherent disqualification — fine,
phrases.notes: Planting does not fix a disqualification of this kind.

phrases.english: but according to the one who says
phrases.notes: Now we look at the opinion where there's a difficulty.

phrases.english: diversion of attention is a disqualification of impurity —
phrases.notes: In that view, it's only a doubt of טומאה, not certain טומאה.

phrases.english: what is there to say?!
phrases.notes: Planting removes certain טומאה, so it should surely remove doubtful טומאה.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר הֶיסַּח הַדַּעַת פְּסוּל הַגּוּף הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב ששת's answer from step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's claim that the saplings stay forbidden to כהנים because of היסח הדעת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר-style argument: if planting purifies certain טומאה, it should surely remove doubtful טומאה. So under the פסול טומאה view, nothing should stay forbidden.

steps.title: The dispute: is היסח הדעת a matter of טומאה or a disqualification of its own?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the dispute behind the challenge: רבי יוחנן says היסח הדעת is פסול טומאה, and רבי שמעון בן לקיש says it is פסול הגוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was stated: About היסח הדעת, רבי יוחנן said it is פסול טומאה, and רבי שמעון בן לקיש said it is פסול הגוף.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows who holds the two views it just mentioned. It quotes an argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This supplies the source for the two views used in step 16. רבי יוחנן holds the view that makes רב ששת's answer hard to explain. ריש לקיש holds the view that fits it well.

phrases.english: As it was stated: diversion of attention —
phrases.notes: Names the topic of the dispute.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: פְּסוּל טוּמְאָה הָוֵי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: it is a disqualification of impurity,
phrases.notes: Based on the worry that it became טמא.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אָמַר: פְּסוּל הַגּוּף הָוֵי.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: it is an inherent disqualification.
phrases.notes: A rule of its own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the two views mentioned in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: היסח הדעת is פסול טומאה. ריש לקיש: היסח הדעת is פסול הגוף.

steps.title: The practical difference: what if אליהו declared it טהור?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows the practical difference between the views. If אליהו came and said the item is טהור, רבי יוחנן says we would listen to him, but ריש לקיש says we would not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said it is פסול טומאה: if אליהו came and declared it טהור, we listen to him. רבי שמעון בן לקיש says it is פסול הגוף: if אליהו came and declared it טהור, we do not listen to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the two views differ in practice, using the example of אליהו הנביא clarifying the facts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן the problem is only a doubt about the facts. If אליהו tells us the item never became טמא, the doubt is gone and the item is fine. For ריש לקיש the rule applies no matter what actually happened, so even true information from אליהו does not help.

keyTerms.meaning: אליהו הנביא, who will come and settle unknown facts
We listen to him; his information is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: פסול טומאה (רבי יוחנן) depends on the facts, so אליהו could remove it. פסול הגוף (ריש לקיש) is a fixed rule, so even אליהו cannot change it. רב ששת's answer fits ריש לקיש easily. It is still hard to explain according to רבי יוחנן.
steps.whyThisMatters: The אליהו test is the classic way to tell a doubt-based rule apart from a fixed rule. The גמרא uses it in many places.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר פְּסוּל טוּמְאָה הָוֵי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said it is a disqualification of impurity:
phrases.notes: Restates his view in order to show its result.

phrases.english: for if Elijah were to come and declare it pure —
phrases.notes: A test case: someone who knows the true facts.

phrases.english: we listen to him.
phrases.notes: The doubt is removed.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אוֹמֵר פְּסוּל הַגּוּף הָוֵי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says it is an inherent disqualification:
for if Elijah were to come and declare it pure —
phrases.notes: The same test case.

phrases.english: we do not listen to him.
phrases.notes: The rule does not depend on the facts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the practical result of the dispute quoted in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוחנן, אליהו's declaration would make it טהור. According to ריש לקיש, it would not.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן quotes a ברייתא about a gap where disqualified birds were left
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש with a ברייתא. It says disqualified bird חטאות were thrown into a small gap by the כבש, left until their form decayed, and then taken out to be burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן raised an objection to רבי שמעון בן לקיש: רבי ישמעאל, the son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא, says: There was a small gap between the ramp and the altar, on the western side of the ramp. That is where they would throw disqualified bird sin-offerings. They stayed there until their form decayed, and then they were taken out to the place of burning.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן brings a ברייתא as an objection to ריש לקיש. Here the גמרא only quotes the source. The step after this explains why it is a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key detail is that the disqualified birds were not burned right away. They had to wait until their form decayed, which means waiting overnight so they become disqualified for sure. רבי יוחנן will use this waiting period against ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: The ramp leading up to the מזבח
Their form decays, meaning they are left overnight until they become disqualified for sure
The place where disqualified קדשים are burned

steps.confusionAlert: 'תעובר צורתן' does not mean the birds rot physically right away. It means they stay overnight so that they become definitely פסול because of לינה (being left past the deadline). Only then may they be burned.

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan raised an objection to Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish:
phrases.notes: This is how the גמרא introduces a challenge from a ברייתא.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָא אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka, says:

phrases.aramaic: לוּל קָטָן הָיָה בֵּין כֶּבֶשׁ לַמִּזְבֵּחַ
phrases.english: There was a small gap between the ramp and the altar
on the western side of the ramp,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁשָּׁם הָיוּ זוֹרְקִין פְּסוּלֵי חַטַּאת הָעוֹף,
phrases.english: where they would throw disqualified bird sin-offerings,
until their form would decay,
phrases.notes: In practice, this means until the next morning.

phrases.english: and then they are taken out to the place of burning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 18 showed the practical difference between the two views. Now רבי יוחנן brings a source that he thinks supports his view and challenges ריש לקיש.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that היסח הדעת is פסול הגוף
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא requires waiting until עיבור צורה before burning. The next step explains why this does not fit ריש לקיש's view.

steps.title: Why wait for decay if the bird is already permanently disqualified?
steps.stepSummary: Waiting until עיבור צורה makes sense if היסח הדעת is only a doubt about טומאה, because אליהו might come and declare the bird טהור. If it is פסול הגוף, there is no reason to wait.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well if you say היסח הדעת is a disqualification because of possible טומאה. That is why it needs to wait for its form to decay: maybe אליהו will come and declare it טהור. But if you say it is a built-in disqualification of the item itself, why do I need to wait for its form to decay?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains why the ברייתא is a problem for ריש לקיש. The waiting period fits his own view but seems pointless according to ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוחנן, the bird is only possibly טמא, so we may not burn קדשים that might really be fine. We wait overnight until it becomes definitely פסול. According to ריש לקיש, the bird is already definitely פסול, so it should be burned immediately.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well if you say
Waiting until the form decays, which makes the item definitely פסול
Perhaps אליהו will come and declare it טהור

steps.whyThisMatters: This step uses the exact practical difference from step 18 (whether אליהו could declare the item טהור) as the basis for an attack. That gives the challenge its force.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא פְּסוּל טוּמְאָה הָוֵי,
phrases.english: It works well if you say it is a disqualification due to impurity,
because of this it requires decay of form,
since perhaps Elijah will come and declare it pure.
But if you say it is an inherent disqualification,
why do I need decay of form?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא פְּסוּל טוּמְאָה הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This step explains how the ברייתא quoted in step 19 challenges ריש לקיש.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that היסח הדעת is פסול הגוף
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Waiting for עיבור צורה only makes sense when the disqualification is uncertain. Under פסול הגוף, the bird is certainly פסול, so waiting is unnecessary.

steps.title: Bringing a משנה to strengthen the challenge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting a משנה that states a general rule, to prove that anything with a פסול הגוף is burned right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: And didn't we learn in a משנה: this is the general rule:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is about to quote a משנה's general rule to back up רבי יוחנן's challenge, and the content continues in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question 'why wait?' is about to be strengthened with an explicit משנה. That משנה will show that an item disqualified in itself is burned immediately, so the waiting in the ברייתא really does contradict ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: And didn't we learn in a mishna: this is the principle:
phrases.notes: The rule itself appears on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This step supports the question in step 20 by bringing a משנה that says an item with פסול הגוף is burned immediately.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that an item with פסול הגוף does not need עיבור צורה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה stating a general rule (quoted on the next amud)
